I have a Pfaff Select 150. It's only the second machine I've had (my first was a cheaper Brother one that I got as a teenager and I used it to death) so I don't have a whole lot to compare it to, but I really like it. My first one was digital and this one isn't, and I kind of prefer it that way. It's a good all-around machine in my opinion- I've heard it's not the best for really light fabrics, but I've never tried to sew any so I've never had any major trouble with it. It does handle heavier fabrics and multiple layers well, which is more my sort of thing. It came with 5 extra presser feet too, which was pretty nice. I've had it nearly three years now.

What about yourselves?

I've gone the industrial sewing route for the most part, I currently have six machines in my garage shop.

Babylock Enterprise, Juki 1540s, Merrow A-3DW, Babylock serger, Singer serger pro 5 and in my office in my house is a home is a Viking 6440 that I'm constantly darning things on or hanging clothes on it that need to be darned.

I have the Singer Talent. I love it. It's sturdy and can be used with almost any fabric type. I sew a lot of canvas which the Talent can handle (except in thick layers). Plus, it's on the less expensive side (~$200).

Hi, I'm new to voat, but I want to be an active member. I have a brother xr4040 it's computerized and all purpose. It's good for either making clothes or quilting. It came with an assortment of feet like a button holer and zipper foot. I like making clothes over quilts. I also have an older brother embroidery machine. I'd have to get up to look at the model number. My gran gave it to me after she got a ten needle machine. In fact, she gave me both of them... my first machine was also a brother, but not computerized and simplistic. I think it was a Wal-Mart special. She gave me the xr4040 as an upgrade. It's something that we both like to do. I wish I had a serger tho

I also have a Brother and I love it. It's the CS 6000i model with about 60 stitches. It's not too complicated for a beginner but has been perfectly adequate for some more advanced and heavy-duty projects.

Aloha! I have an older hand me down from my dad. He took up sewing for a bit when I was younger. It's easily 25 years old and still rocking. It's definitely time for a new one though... And I have a baby lock serger. I'm very excited to be a part of this community,
